subject: INLA equivalent of mgcv's factor smooth basis

messages.author: 34560e4cfcedfadd
messages.subject: INLA equivalent of mgcv's factor smooth basis
parts:
I'm in the process of learning INLA in order to adapt an existing GAMM from mgcv, but I can't figure out the equivalent to mgcv's s(…, bs="fs") smooth random effects. The model specification in mgcv is 

m1_approx <- gamm(y ~  x + s(time, by=x, bs="cr", k = 40) + s(time, ID, bs="fs", k=5), data=df),

where x and ID are factor variables. 

Incidentally, are there existing methods for adaptive spline random effects? The functional observations I'm modelling exhibit varying degrees of smoothness over time with each observation having different patterns of smoothness.

I'm not presicely sure of the mgcv format for s(), but we use a
continous time formulation for 'splines', usually, you would like
model="rw2", and add scale.model=TRUE to make it standarized. I do not
know what the 'factor' do in s() though...

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] INLA equivalent of mgcv's factor smooth basis
parts: The factor in the first term creates a smooth term in time for each level of x with its own smoothing parameters. The second term creates a smooth term in time for every level of ID, but all share the same set of smoothing parameters.

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] INLA equivalent of mgcv's factor smooth basis
parts:
So I'm testing this model on simulated data generated from a random slope and intercept model with two groups with the same underlying mean function differing by an additive constant. The smooth random effect model inferences should roughly match the actual model. The reference model produces estimates consistent with the simulated data:

formula1 <- y ~  factor(x) + f(time_x1, model="rw2") + f(time_x2, model="rw2") + f(id, model="iid2d", n=2*nid) + f(slopeid, time, copy="id"),

I've defined time_x1 to be time when x == 1 and NA otherwise, similarly for time_x2.

However my smooth random effect model, with smooth random effects per level of id governed by a single smoothing parameter, produces a fit that does not make sense. The formula I used is

formula2 <- y ~  factor(x) + f(time_x1, model="rw2") + f(time_x2, model="rw2") + f(time, model="rw2", replicate = id)

I'm not sure I understand how to use the replicate argument.

And if you would have a lot of levels, the model probably wouldn't make sense ;-)

parts: OK after some tinkering I think I figured it out. I think the issue is that I forgot that the term f(time, method="rw2", replicate=id) has a sum-to-zero constraint so it couldn't model additive deviations from the group effects. To address this I added a random intercept term, so the model reads
y ~ factor(x) + f(time_x1, model="rw2") + f(time_x2, model="rw2") +

f(id, model="iid") + f(time, model="rw2", replicate=id)

This yields estimates that agree with the random slope and intercept model without assuming linear random effects.

Incidentally, a model that works equally well is one using AR1 random effects:
y ~ factor(x) + f(time_x1, model="rw2") + f(time_x2, model="rw2") +

f(time, model="ar1", replicate=id)

Here we don't need to have an "iid" effect since it's already incorporated into the "ar1" model.

I hope this is helpful to someone in the future. If I'm misunderstanding anything please let me know. Thanks for the help!
